source.title: Adversarial Parameter Defense by Multi-Step Risk Minimization
source.authors: Zhiyuan Zhang; Ruixuan Luo; Xuancheng Ren; Qi Su; Liangyou Li; Xu Sun

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains models with parameter-corruption defense and reports clean evaluation performance, testing whether a parameter-robustness intervention changes generalization. Its measures and intervention do not match any listed version closely enough to link rows to one.
record.gate_note: The study reports clean evaluation scores and parameter-corruption robustness. The corruption results measure robustness to parameter changes, not the natural-label train/test gap, so they are not extracted as rows for these claim versions. The study's cited generalization results are not its own results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minima/generalization connection to motivate a parameter-defense method and reports that method's clean performance and corruption robustness. It tests none of V1–V8. In particular, its absolute-norm perturbations and conditional generalization bound do not test V7's magnitude-scaled sharpness ranking of measured generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors conclude that their defense improves clean performance and robustness against several parameter-corruption methods, random noise, and quantization. They explicitly interpret the clean-performance gains as better generalization and provide a conditional theoretical bound, but report no measured train/test gaps. They also acknowledge that defending the whole model leaves some layers vulnerable.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains with a multi-step adversarial parameter corruption risk objective; it does not reproduce the methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that results vary with corruption radius, number of steps, norm constraint, initialization, dataset/task, and which layers are defended. Its De-En setting study reports that performance first increases and then drops as K or corruption magnitude increases; zero initialization outperforms random initialization in tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed defense raises clean scores from 94.46 to 96.34 accuracy on CIFAR-10, 74.90 to 75.77 mAP on VOC, 30.64 to 31.09 BLEU on En-Vi, 35.32 to 35.88 BLEU on De-En, and 92.03 to 92.78 development accuracy on SST-2. The authors report significant baseline comparisons using three runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-step adversarial parameter defense can improve clean held-out performance in these tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.3 bounds population error using training error, absolute-norm parameter-loss changes, and a complexity term under stated assumptions. This does not establish an empirical ranking by magnitude-aware sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-corruption loss indicators enter a conditional PAC-Bayes generalization bound.

record.problems: The study reports clean evaluation scores but not training error or train/test gaps, so the scores cannot establish a change in generalization gap. Clean performance experiments were repeated 3 times; the paper reports a Student-t test with n = 3. SST-2 uses development sentences as the test set.
record.rows_left_out: Parameter-corruption robustness results and comparisons across corruption methods and strengths are not included as rows because they measure corruption robustness rather than a listed version's named outcome. Those results appear in Table 1 and Tables 3, 5, and 6.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning; different tasks use different optimizers without a controlled comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, dropout strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance ranking measured train/test gaps at similarly low training loss, including comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Clean held-out scores are valid performance outcomes; their exclusion follows from the specific claim versions, not merely the lack of training-error measurements. All extracted rows concern the study's own method evaluation. No version-level verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with fitting natural labels.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on generalization; optimizer comparisons are not the focus.
Does not test dropout's effect on held-out error.
Measures robustness to parameter corruption, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness as a ranking of train/test gaps among networks with similarly low training loss.
